clue.text: Reportedly how to get boot on troublesome creature?

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: you get a boot on by using a shoehorn, so you 'horn it'

explanation.surface: A riddle about getting your footwear on while some pest bothers you.
explanation.walkthrough: To ease a boot on you 'horn it' with a shoehorn; said out loud that matches the stinging insect.
explanation.definitionFit: This large wasp is a stinging insect that can be a real nuisance.

clue.text: Male fellow is the first pleasure seeker

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: the first picks the opening letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A male academic is the first to go looking for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first' takes T, the first letter of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to pleasure as life's chief aim pursues enjoyment above all.

clue.text: Back a drug's disposal as this kind of action?

parts.note: rear means back

indicators.note: disposal is read as arrangement, so the letters of a drug are laid out afresh

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a drug from the back of a cupboard, in some military defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposal' rearranges A DRUG (the 's is no letter) into GUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive fight by retreating troops protecting the rear is the military term for that action.

clue.text: Reverberation in the choir

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the words the choir

explanation.surface: Sound resounding among the singers of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound reflected back off a surface is a resounding repeat.

clue.text: Frequently she upsets people who are new to college

indicators.note: upsets says the three letters of she are knocked into a new order

parts.note: men is a general word for people

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps annoying the first-year students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' turns SHE into ESH, which sits between FR and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: First-year students at a college or university are called this in the US and elsewhere.

clue.text: Sorrow about code

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Morse is the dot-and-dash telegraph code

explanation.surface: Grief over a secret cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep regret for wrongdoing is a kind of sorrow.

clue.text: Car lamp set, when decrepit, to be this?

definitions.text: Car lamp set, when decrepit, to be this?

indicators.note: decrepit means worn out and broken down, so the letters of car lamp set fall apart into a new order

explanation.surface: Old car lights end up as junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when decrepit' rearranges CAR LAMP SET, and the whole clue describes what worn-out car parts become.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded metal parts sold for recycling are what a worn-out car lamp set would be.

clue.text: Greek character to fit out in ordinary clothes

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: out signals the letters of fit are put out of order

explanation.surface: Kitting out a Greek in everyday wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns FIT into FTI after MU.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain civilian dress worn by someone usually in uniform is called this.

clue.text: Desmond, run over, would have to be this?

definitions.text: Desmond, run over, would have to be this?

indicators.note: over says the words are turned back to front

parts.note: Des is the short form of the name Desmond
run taken as written

explanation.surface: A man knocked down by a car needs caring for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DES RUN round; the whole clue says what an injured Desmond would need.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hurt in an accident would be looked after and cared for while recovering.

clue.text: Used to be that woman's laundress

parts.note: was is the past tense of be
her is the possessive meaning that woman's

explanation.surface: Explaining that a certain woman had once done laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who launders clothes does the cleaning, so the word for one who cleans fits.

clue.text: Badly paid by hour to edit mag showing muscular structure

indicators.note: badly says the letters of paid are put in a poor, jumbled order
to edit something is to rework it, so the letters of mag are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poorly paid hourly worker employed to edit a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' turns PAID into DIAP and 'to edit' turns MAG into AGM, with HR in between.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheet of muscle separating chest from abdomen, used in breathing, is a muscular structure.

clue.text: Look up and equally from side to side

indicators.note: the word reads the same from either side, which is what equally from side to side describes

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Consult a reference book, reading the page evenly left and right.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half of the clue simply says the answer is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: To consult a dictionary or a source is to look something up.

clue.text: Pesters Arabs?

explanation.surface: A question whether Arabs are nuisances.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pesters keeps on at you; Arabs are a breed of horse, and old horses are called by the same word.

clue.text: Does it represent investment in the harvest?

definitions.text: Does it represent investment in the harvest?

parts.words: Does it represent investment in the harvest
parts.note: a share of the harvest might seem to have a cost, but the phrase is really the market value of a single unit of stock in a company

explanation.surface: A farmer wondering what his stake in the crop is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: The market value of one unit of stock reflects what an investor pays to hold part of a company.

clue.text: English article I insist is having heavenly effect

parts.note: the is the definite article
really can be an emphatic interjection meaning I insist

explanation.surface: An English grammarian insisting a word works divinely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in a delicate, otherworldly way has a celestial quality.

clue.text: Vague threats remove one's peace of mind

indicators.note: vague suggests something unclear and ill-formed, so the letters of threats are scrambled

explanation.surface: Unspecific threats can still leave someone anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone badly is to wreck their calm, destroying their composure.

clue.text: French pupil's joining new team

parts.note: eleve is the French word for a pupil

explanation.surface: A French schoolboy gets into a newly formed side.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket and football sides have this many players, so the number stands for a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side fields this number of players, so the number names the side.

clue.text: Detective and what he might have to do to get cosmetic

parts.note: a private eye is a detective

parts.words: what he might have to do
parts.note: a detective may shadow, or follow, a suspect

explanation.surface: A sleuth trailing someone ends up with make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured powder applied to the eyelids is a piece of make-up.

clue.text: After time in prison has yen to be flexible

parts.note: a stretch is slang for a prison sentence
Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Coming out of jail with a longing to be adaptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic can be pulled out and returns, so it bends without breaking.

clue.text: Pay attention to publicity

explanation.surface: Notice the marketing material.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to something is a formal way to refer or attend to it; an ad is a piece of publicity.

clue.text: Animal has to go wrong in row

indicators.note: in says one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: A creature makes a mistake in a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of small dog bred to hunt burrowing creatures is an animal.

clue.text: One needs help before lecture in non-standard language

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'One needs help before lecture', gives no letters for DIALECT: DIA as help turned round has no reversal indicator, and nothing in 'lecture' gives LECT without a truncation signal; looks cut or misread.
annotationWithheld.clue: One needs help before lecture in non-standard language

clue.text: A hazard in untidy garden

indicators.note: untidy suggests things out of place, so the letters of garden are mixed up

explanation.surface: A messy garden is a risk to visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A source of risk or peril counts as a threat.

clue.text: Was nosey about male made ready for work

indicators.note: about says the nosy word goes round the male

parts.note: pried means was nosey

explanation.surface: Someone snooped on a man getting prepared for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepared and set up in advance, as a pump or a surface before painting.

clue.text: Embarrassed by woman's call; this can divert one's attention

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face
her is the possessive for a woman
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Blushing at a phone call from a woman distracts you.
explanation.walkthrough: A false clue planted to mislead, named after a smoked fish once dragged to throw hounds off a scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleading clue planted to distract from the truth is the classic diversion in a mystery story.

clue.text: Kind of architecture featuring unit covered in ornate cord

indicators.note: covered in says the unit is wrapped within the other letters
ornate suggests elaborate twisting, so the letters of cord are rearranged

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, is a unit

explanation.surface: A building style that features cord decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ornate' rearranges CORD into DORC, and 'covered in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The plainest of the classical Greek orders is a style of columns and buildings.

clue.text: Small house in south-east where old woman lived?

indicators.note: in places the small house within the compass direction

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east
HO is the abbreviation for house, and small signals the shortening

explanation.surface: A cottage in the south-east of England once home to an elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'There was an old woman who lived in a ...' gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the old woman with so many children lived inside an item of footwear.

clue.text: See fellow become unwell and do badly in exam

parts.note: to ail is to be or become unwell

explanation.surface: A student feeling sick does poorly in a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Not reaching the pass mark means doing badly in a test.

clue.text: Ancient city features in bad French painting

indicators.note: features in says one piece appears within another

parts.note: mal is the French word for bad
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An old city appears in a poorly executed French picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall painting is a large artwork applied directly to a wall.

clue.text: Integrated circuits attached round animal from Northern country

indicators.note: attached round says the circuits are fixed on either side of the animal

parts.note: IC is the abbreviation for integrated circuit, and the plural gives two of them
an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: Electronics fitted around a beast from the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'circuits' supplies two ICs, one each side of ELAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the Nordic island nation in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Shorten by three feet in Rosyth?

parts.note: to dock a tail is to shorten it
a yard measures three feet

explanation.surface: Cutting something down by a yard in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosyth, on the Firth of Forth in Scotland, is a naval shipyard, so it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosyth in Fife is a well-known naval shipbuilding and repair yard, an example of the type.

clue.text: Gradually get cunning, taking in wise type?

indicators.note: taking in says the wise type is placed inside the cunning word

parts.note: sly means cunning
the owl is the traditional emblem of wisdom

explanation.surface: Over time someone becomes crafty after befriending a sage.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by degrees means doing it without haste.
